title: Service Stop
summary: Service stop is the deliberate shutdown or disabling of a service or process so that the function it provides becomes unavailable. Attackers use it for three related reasons: to interrupt incident response by taking security and monitoring agents offline, to free locked data stores so they can be encrypted or overwritten, and purely to deny a business function such as mail or database access. On Windows the mechanism is the service control manager or a registry edit that changes the start type, so the service never returns after a reboot. In cloud environments the equivalent is an interface call that disables a managed service or blocks it from creating the roles it needs. Evidence sits in service state change events, in configuration records showing a start type of disabled, and in the pattern of many services stopping on many hosts within a very short window.

beginner.definition: A service is a program that runs in the background to provide something, such as email, file sharing or printing. This technique means an attacker stops those services so nobody can use them. Sometimes the service is only stopped for a moment, and sometimes it is switched off for good.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stopping security services blinds your defenders during an attack. Stopping mail or database services stops the business and can cause angry customers and lost money. Some services lock their files while running, so attackers stop them first to change the data on disk. A short outage can also be a warning sign of something much bigger coming next.
howItWorks: The attacker gets administrator rights on a machine, or rights over a cloud service configuration.
They list the running services and pick security tools, mail, database, or backup services to target.
They send a stop command through the service manager, a command line tool, or a script.
For a permanent effect they change the service start type to disabled so it never returns.
With the service offline, its files are unlocked and can be encrypted or overwritten.
The same step repeats across the network so the whole organisation loses the function.
beginner.example: Think of a hotel at night. The night manager relies on the door alarm, the key card system and the booking computer. An intruder who can switch those three things off at the fuse box can walk the corridors and change the records without anybody arguing. Even if the alarm is switched back on in an hour, the intruder has already done what they came for.
takeaways: Alert on security and backup services stopping, especially outside maintenance windows.
A cluster of service stops on many hosts at once is almost never a coincidence.
Record service start types so you can see when one has been set to disabled.

objectives: Explain what a service is and why attackers target services.
Describe the three main reasons attackers stop or disable services.
Identify the telemetry that records a service stopping or changing its start type.
Explain how stopping a service unlocks data for later encryption or destruction.
Describe the cloud equivalent of stopping a service and how to audit it.
Explain why widespread simultaneous service stops suggest a coordinated attack.
